record.paper_title: Norming Markushevich bases: recent results and open problems
record.original_question: Let X be a Banach space. (1) If X has a norming Markushevich basis, must the dual ball (B_{X*},w*) be semi-Eberlein? (2) If (B_{X*},w*) is semi-Eberlein for every equivalent renorming of X, must X be a subspace of a weakly compactly generated Banach space? (3) Are the dual balls of C([0,ω₁]) and of C(K_ρ) semi-Eberlein?

evidence.quote: Problem 7.4. (1) Let X be a Banach space with norming M-basis. Must (BX∗, w∗) be semi-Eberlein? (2) Assume that (BX∗, w∗) is semi-Eberlein for every renorming of X. Is X a subspace of a WCG Banach space? (3) Are the dual balls of C([0, ω1]) or C(Kϱ) semi-Eberlein?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Preliminaries. Let X be a (real) Banach space with closed unit ball B_X and topological dual X*. The weak* topology on X* is denoted w*. A biorthogonal system {(x_α, x*_α) : α ∈ Γ} ⊂ X × X* is a Markushevich basis (M-basis) of X if span{x_α : α ∈ Γ} is dense in X and {x*_α : α ∈ Γ} separates the points of X. An M-basis is called norming if the closed linear subspace span‖·‖{x*_α : α ∈ Γ} of X* is a norming subspace of X*, i.e., the formula |||x||| = sup{|x*(x)| : x* ∈ span{x*_α}, ‖x*‖ ≤ 1} defines an equivalent norm on X.

A compact Hausdorff space K is called Eberlein if it is homeomorphic to a weakly compact subset of some Banach space. K is called semi-Eberlein if there exists a set D ⊂ K which is dense in K and such that D is homeomorphic to a subset of some Σ-product of real lines that consists of points with countable support — equivalently, K contains a dense subset whose points each "depend on countably many coordinates" in a topological embedding of K into some [-1,1]^Γ. A Banach space X is weakly compactly generated (WCG) if there exists a weakly compact subset W ⊂ X with X = span‖·‖ W. Let ω_1 denote the first uncountable ordinal, equipped with the order topology on [0, ω_1], so that C([0, ω_1]) is the Banach space of continuous real functions with sup-norm. Let K_ϱ denote the following compact space: take an Aronszajn tree T (a tree of height ω_1 with countable levels and no uncountable branches or antichains) and let K_ϱ be the one-point compactification of T (with the tree-interval topology), or equivalently the standard compactification associated with the ϱ-function construction of Todorčević. 

Problem. 
(1) If X is a Banach space possessing a norming Markushevich basis, must the dual ball (B_{X*}, w*) be a semi-Eberlein compact space?
(2) Suppose that for every equivalent norm |||·||| on X the dual ball (B_{(X,|||·|||)*}, w*) is semi-Eberlein. Does it follow that X is isomorphic to a subspace of some weakly compactly generated Banach space?
(3) Are the dual balls (B_{C([0,ω_1])*}, w*) and (B_{C(K_ϱ)*}, w*) semi-Eberlein compact spaces?
artifact.status_search_result: A 2024 survey on norming M-bases lists these three questions as open problems (Problem 7.4). Search results show ongoing related work (e.g., on Banach spaces of continuous functions without norming M-bases, 2023; quasi-greedy M-bases and norming subspaces, 2025) but no resolution of the three semi-Eberlein dual-ball questions. No source asserts they have been solved.

status_evidence.title: Norming Markushevich bases: recent results and open problems
status_evidence.snippet: Surveys results on norming M-bases and states open problems including Problem 7.4 on semi-Eberlein dual balls.
status_evidence.claim: The three questions are posed together as an open problem in this 2024 survey.

status_evidence.title: Banach spaces of continuous functions without norming Markushevich bases
status_evidence.snippet: Studies which C(K) spaces admit norming M-bases.
status_evidence.claim: Related recent work, does not resolve the semi-Eberlein dual-ball questions.

status_evidence.snippet: 2025 paper studying norming subspaces in connection with M-bases.
status_evidence.claim: Recent activity in the area; no resolution announced.
